data.title: Distinct perturbation of the translatome by the antidiabetic drug metformin
data.authors: Larsson O; Morita M; Topisirovic I; Alain T; Blouin MJ; Pollak M; Sonenberg N

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.model_system: Human cancer cell line (per MeSH); genome-wide polysome microarray translatome analysis comparing metformin, rapamycin and PP242
data.finding: The authors compared genome-wide changes in mRNA translation caused by metformin with those caused by the mTOR inhibitors rapamycin and PP242 in cancer cells. Metformin changed gene expression at the level of translation to an extent comparable to the classic mTOR inhibitors. Its antiproliferative effect could be explained by selective suppression of translation of mRNAs encoding cell-cycle regulators, acting through the mTORC1 / 4E-BP pathway. The paper provided evidence that metformin's effect on cell growth in vitro goes through selective translational control rather than a general drop in protein synthesis. Boundary: Cultured cancer cells at drug concentrations used in vitro; does not show that metformin at clinical doses acts this way in patients. Drafted from the abstract only.
data.abstract_excerpt: Metformin has been reported to lower cancer incidence among type II diabetics. Metformin exhibits antiproliferative and antineoplastic effects associated with inhibition of mammalian target of rapamycin complex 1 (mTORC1), but the mechanisms are poorly understood. We provide a unique genome-wide analysis of translational targets of canonical mTOR inhibitors (rapamycin and PP242) compared with metformin, revealing that metformin controls gene expression at the level of mRNA translation to an extent comparable to that of canonical mTOR inhibitors.

extracted_findings.target: Genome-wide mRNA translation (translatome); cell-cycle regulator mRNAs; proliferation
extracted_findings.effect: Metformin selectively suppresses translation of cell-cycle regulator mRNAs via mTORC1/4E-BP, reducing proliferation
